title: remobi.app: Don't change your terminal workflow for mobile
talk_summary: A demo of remobi.app, a progressive web app that exposes an existing tmux session (with multiple coding agents, git/lazygit, custom keybindings) to a phone over Tailscale, so the user keeps their terminal workflow instead of adopting a vendor-specific mobile app. The talk is mostly a personal-workflow show-and-tell with no measured results.

takeaways.technique: Persistent tmux session as the agent workspace
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs several coding agents in parallel panes/windows inside one long-lived tmux session on a remote dev box, with custom keybindings and status widgets, and attaches to it from any client.
takeaways.evidence_quote: why not have four different coding agents on there at the same time? And so, what tmux is is essentially like a window manager for your terminal

takeaways.technique: Skill that installs and configures the tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a copy-paste shell script, ships an agent skill that detects whether tmux exists, installs it if not, and generates keybindings for the user's setup.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it installs a skill that helps you set up tmux if you haven't got it already. Or if you've got tmux, it turns it into key bindings

takeaways.what_they_do: Exposes the local agent server to the phone only over Tailscale/Cloudflare tunnels, explicitly warning that public exposure means compromise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you just put it on the public internet, you've pwned your computer.
